questions.title: What does this loop with setTimeout print with var, and how does let change it?
questions.quick: With var the loop prints 3, 3, 3. var is function scoped, so there is a single i shared by all callbacks, and by the time the timers fire after the synchronous loop, i is 3. With let it prints 0, 1, 2, because let creates a fresh binding for each iteration and each callback closes over its own copy. Older fixes are an immediately invoked function that captures the value, or passing the value as a setTimeout argument.
questions.revision: var shares one i across callbacks, so timers print 3,3,3 after the loop ends. let creates a new binding per iteration, so 0,1,2.
